questions.title: Who will win Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election?
questions.background: Okinawa is Japan's southernmost prefecture, where the presence of US military bases is a major political issue.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official results announced by Okinawa's election authorities, either directly or as reported by reliable news organizations. Resolution : The question resolves when the winner of Okinawa's 2026 gubernatorial election is officially announced. Accepted Answer Format : The winning candidate's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-08-27/28 official campaign kickoff update (Ryukyu Shimpo Aug 27, Japan Times Aug 27, QAB News Aug 28): Candidate filing closed at 5:00 PM on Aug 27 with six confirmed candidates and early voting beginning today (Aug 28), and crucially former MP Mikio Shimoji DID NOT FILE (removed from 0.02 -> 0.00; the other four entrants are minor candidates). Shimoji's withdrawal removes the key conservative spoiler who won 53,677 votes (8%) in 2022 and was judged by LDP insiders to siphon votes primarily from challenger Genta Koja. Koja enters the official campaign backed by an expanded six-party bloc (LDP, Ishin, DPFP, Sanseito, Conservative Party, and Komeito Okinawa chapter), while an LDP internal poll progression reported Aug 20-21 (prior to Shimoji's exit) showed Tamaki's lead narrowing steadily from 9 points in early July to 6 points in early August to 4.4 points (45.5% vs 41.1%) in mid-August amid heightened focus on inflation/economy. Balancing Tamaki's two-term incumbency and persistent narrow polling lead against Koja's united conservative/centrist coalition without Shimoji, we tighten the race to a near-even toss-up: Denny Tamaki 0.50 (down from 0.54) vs Genta Koja 0.49 (up from 0.43), leaving 0.01 across the four minor candidates.

questions.title: Which country will Washington propose as a possible venue for renewed trilateral Russia–Ukraine ceasefire talks by September 25, 2026?
questions.background: The United States has been involved in efforts to broker an end to the Russia–Ukraine war.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country publicly identified by Ukraine's president as Washington's proposed location for renewed talks involving the United States, Russia and Ukraine, using the proposal current as of September 25, 2026. A suggested location is sufficient; the talks need not have taken place. Resolution Date : 2026-09-25 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Rebalancing venue probabilities after late-August diplomatic developments while talks remain formally unscheduled (Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov stated on Aug 28 that Moscow has no direct info on September trilateral talks, though top Ukrainian adviser Kyrylo Budanov said Aug 28 he expects 'technical talks' very soon and Zelenskyy confirmed US briefings after CIA Director John Ratcliffe's Aug 25 Moscow visit). Turkey rises (0.24 -> 0.28) as the Kremlin confirmed on Aug 28 that Putin will hold bilateral talks on the Ukraine war with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan at the Aug 31-Sep 1 SCO summit in Bishkek, building on Ankara hosting the July 2026 NATO summit where Trump met Zelenskyy and Istanbul's established mediation role. United Arab Emirates (0.14 -> 0.11) and Saudi Arabia (0.09 -> 0.07) are trimmed because the US-Iran 60-day ceasefire memorandum expired Aug 17 without a deal, keeping Persian Gulf military tensions elevated; 0.14 remains outside the top 5 (Austria, Azerbaijan, Hungary, Qatar, Italy/Vatican).

questions.title: Which country will be the first in 2026 to publicly acknowledge deploying purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit?
questions.background: Military satellites provide communications, navigation and intelligence services. Deploying weapons in orbit could significantly change how countries protect or threaten these systems.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements by national governments or military officials, corroborated by reliable international news reporting. Qualifying Event : Resolve to the country whose government or military first publicly acknowledges during 2026 that it has already deployed purpose-built weapons in Earth orbit. Merely describing satellites with potential military applications, announcing future deployments, or confirming ground-based anti-satellite weapons does not qualify. Resolution Timing : Resolve on the date of the first qualifying public acknowledgment, provided it occurs by December 31, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No country had publicly acknowledged already-deployed orbital weapons as of Aug 25, 2026. However, Aug 14 reporting (Asia Times / The War Zone) revealed a notable US doctrinal shift: US SPACECOM Commander Gen. Stephen Whiting announced offensive kinetic and non-kinetic ASAT capabilities ('integrated space fires' and counter-pLEO) as a top military priority, with US defense officials explicitly stressing the joint force must possess a 'credible, acknowledged ability' to attack adversary space assets (while noting the ground-based CCS jammer remains the only publicly acknowledged US offensive ASAT to date). Meanwhile, Aug 8 reporting on Golden Dome confirmed $3.2B for space-based interceptor prototypes targeting late-2026 tests and 2027 flight demos (future, not yet deployed). With Pentagon leadership openly building the case for public acknowledgment ahead of the mid-September AFA Air, Space & Cyber Conference, US probability rises from 0.42 to 0.49 while Russia (0.25, active co-orbital ASAT testing), China (0.12), France (0.08), and India (0.03) remain key alternatives.

questions.title: Who will top the PSA women's world squash rankings on September 21, 2026?
questions.background: The Professional Squash Association (PSA) publishes weekly world rankings for professional squash players.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The official PSA women's world rankings dated September 21, 2026. Resolution : Resolve to the player ranked first in that rankings update. Accepted Answer Format : The player's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Official August 2026 PSA Squash Tour and Gulf Times draw releases clarify that TWO major ranking events occur before the Sept 21 rankings update (rather than one as assumed in June): the Gold-level London Squash Classic (Sept 1-6) and the Platinum-level QTerminals Qatar Classic (Sept 12-18). World No. 1 Hania El Hammamy remains favored (90.4% win rate in 2025/26, defending 2025 Qatar champion, with upside in London where World No. 2 Amina Orfi is defending champion). However, Orfi's overtake odds are materially higher than 0.23: she won the 2026 World Championships and British Open (beating El Hammamy), led the tour in % of points won (61.8% vs 59.6%), came within one match of #1 at June's Tour Finals, and PSA previews highlight Doha as her immediate shot at #1—especially with El Hammamy facing returning former #1 Nouran Gohar in the Qatar quarter-finals. Meanwhile, Gohar (returning at #6 seed after a 1-year absence, skipping London) has virtually no mathematical path to #1 by Sept 21, and Nour El Sherbini (skipping London, #3 seed in Qatar) has only a remote tail chance (0.015). Accordingly, we shift El Hammamy 0.72 -> 0.63, Orfi 0.23 -> 0.35, El Sherbini 0.03 -> 0.015, and drop Gohar.
